source_refs.note: Book p. 13-14: second '1.5.2 Inverse Hyperbolic Functions' (shown as 1.5.4): (i) sinh^-1 with Note box and Example 10, (ii) cosh^-1 with Remember! box and Example 11

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Kitab is heading ko "1.5.2 Inverse Hyperbolic Functions" chhapti hai: number 1.5.2 bhi dohraya gaya hai aur 1.5.3 ka title bhi. Yahan hum ne ise 1.5.4 number diya hai taa ke har sub-heading ka apna number ho. Yeh page inverse hyperbolic functions ko aage barhata hai: yahan \(\sinh^{-1} x\) aur \(\cosh^{-1} x\) ke formulas derive kiye jate hain.

Pichle page par humne inverse hyperbolic functions ka poora table dekha tha. Ab hum un mein se do sab se ahem formulas khud bana kar dekhenge: \(\sinh^{-1} x\) aur \(\cosh^{-1} x\). Jab aap ek dafa yeh tareeqa samajh lenge to baqi chaar (Exercise 1.2, Question 8) khud ba khud aasan lagenge.

Kitab kehti hai: \(y = \sinh x\) ke graph (Figure 1.8) se horizontal line test ke zariye saaf hai ke yeh function bijective hai. Is liye is ka inverse function mojood hai, aur hum use is tarah define karte hain:
\[x = \sinh^{-1} y \iff y = \sinh x\]
Yani "\(\sinh^{-1} y\) woh number hai jis ka \(\sinh\), \(y\) ke barabar ho".

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text: Agar \(y = f(x)\) ek bijective function hai, to \(x = f^{-1}(y)\) us ka inverse hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Horizontal line test kya hai? Graph par koi bhi seedhi leti hui (horizontal) line \(y = c\) kheenchiye. Agar woh graph ko zyada se zyada ek jagah kaate, to function one-to-one hai. Aur agar har horizontal line graph ko kaate (yani har \(c\) function ki value ho), to function onto hai. One-to-one aur onto dono hon to bijective, aur sirf bijective function ka inverse function hota hai.
Misaal: ek class mein har student ka roll number alag ho aur har roll number kisi student ka ho, to roll number se student wapas pehchana ja sakta hai. Yahi inverse hai.
\(y = \sinh x\) ke liye Figure 1.8 ko har horizontal line bilkul ek dafa kaatti hai, is liye \(\sinh^{-1}\) poore \(\mathbb{R}\) par define hai.
Ab kitab ki pehli misaal, jis mein \(\sinh^{-1} x\) ka formula banta hai:

blocks.title: Example 10
steps:
Diya gaya: \(y = \sinh x\), \(\mathbb{R}\) se \(\mathbb{R}\) par bijection hai, is liye \(\sinh^{-1} x\) har real \(x\) ke liye mojood hai.
Maloom karna (prove karna): \(\sinh^{-1} x = \ln\left(x + \sqrt{x^{2}+1}\right)\).
Tareeqa: \(y = \sinh^{-1} x\) rakhenge, to \(x = \sinh y\). Phir \(\sinh y\) ko \(e^{y}\) mein likhenge; is se \(e^{y}\) ki quadratic equation banegi. Use hal karenge, jo root \(e^{y}\) ho hi nahin sakta use chhor denge, aur aakhir mein \(\ln\) lenge. Yeh tareeqa saare inverse hyperbolic formulas ke liye chalta hai, is liye ise dil se samajh lijiye.

Qadam 1: Inverse ko function mein badliye
Maan lijiye \(y = \sinh^{-1} x\), jahan \(x, y \in\, ]-\infty, \infty[\). To
\[x = \sinh y\]
Kyun: definition ke mutabiq \(y = \sinh^{-1} x\) tabhi hota hai jab \(x = \sinh y\). \(\sinh^{-1}\) ke saath humein kaam karna nahin aata, magar \(\sinh\) ki definition humein maloom hai. Is liye mushkil cheez ko aasan cheez mein badal diya.

Qadam 2: Exponentials mein likhiye
\[x = \dfrac{e^{y} - e^{-y}}{2}\]
\[2x = e^{y} - \dfrac{1}{e^{y}}\]
Kyun: pehle \(\sinh\) ki definition lagai, phir dono taraf 2 se multiply kiya, aur \(e^{-y} = \frac{1}{e^{y}}\) likha taa ke sirf ek hi unknown \(e^{y}\) nazar aaye.

Qadam 3: Fraction khatam kijiye
\[2x = \dfrac{e^{2y} - 1}{e^{y}}\]
\[2xe^{y} = e^{2y} - 1\]
\[(e^{y})^{2} - 2xe^{y} - 1 = 0\]
Kyun: \(e^{y}\) se multiply kiya (yeh kabhi zero nahin hota, is liye mehfooz hai). Ab \(e^{2y} = (e^{y})^{2}\), to agar \(e^{y}\) ko ek naya naam \(u\) de dein to equation \(u^{2} - 2xu - 1 = 0\) ban jati hai: ek seedhi quadratic, jis mein \(a = 1\), \(b = -2x\), \(c = -1\).

Qadam 4: Quadratic formula lagaiye
\[e^{y} = \dfrac{2x \pm \sqrt{4x^{2} + 4}}{2}\]
\[= x \pm \sqrt{x^{2} + 1}\]
Kyun: \(u = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^{2} - 4ac}}{2a}\). Yahan \(b^{2} - 4ac = 4x^{2} - 4(1)(-1) = 4x^{2} + 4\). Phir \(\sqrt{4x^{2}+4} = \sqrt{4(x^{2}+1)} = 2\sqrt{x^{2}+1}\), aur upar neeche ka 2 cancel ho gaya.

Qadam 5: Sahi sign chuniye
Ghor kijiye ke har \(x\) ke liye \(x - \sqrt{x^{2}+1} < 0\). Aur \(e^{y} > 0\) hamesha hota hai. Is liye positive sign hi lena hoga:
\[e^{y} = x + \sqrt{x^{2}+1}\]
Kyun: \(\sqrt{x^{2}+1}\) hamesha \(\sqrt{x^{2}} = |x|\) se bara hai, aur \(|x| \ge x\). To \(x\) mein se us se bari cheez minus karein to jawab negative hi aayega. Magar \(e\) ki koi bhi power kabhi negative nahin hoti. Is liye minus wala root bekaar hai.
Dhyan dein: dono roots ko jawab mein rakhna aam ghalti hai; \(e^{y}\) ka negative hona na-mumkin hai.

Qadam 6: ln lijiye
\[y = \ln\left(x + \sqrt{x^{2}+1}\right)\]
Yani \(\sinh^{-1} x = \ln\left(x + \sqrt{x^{2}+1}\right)\).
Kyun: \(\ln\) aur \(e\) ek doosre ko khatam karte hain: agar \(e^{y} = A\) (aur \(A > 0\)) to \(y = \ln A\). Aakhir mein \(y\) ki jagah wapas \(\sinh^{-1} x\) likh diya.

Tasdeeq: \(x = \frac{3}{4}\) lijiye. \(\sqrt{\frac{9}{16} + 1} = \sqrt{\frac{25}{16}} = \frac{5}{4}\), to formula \(y = \ln\left(\frac{3}{4} + \frac{5}{4}\right) = \ln 2\) deta hai.
\[\sinh(\ln 2) = \dfrac{2 - \frac{1}{2}}{2} = \dfrac{3}{4}\]
Bilkul wahi \(x\) wapas aa gaya. Aur \(x = 0\) par \(\ln 1 = 0\), jab ke \(\sinh 0 = 0\). Formula pakka sahi hai.
blocks.answer: \(\sinh^{-1} x = \ln\left(x + \sqrt{x^{2}+1}\right)\), har real \(x\) ke liye (saabit ho gaya).

blocks.text:
Kitab kehti hai: \(y = \cosh x\) ke graph (Figure 1.9) se horizontal line test ke zariye saaf hai ke yeh function poore domain \((-\infty, \infty)\) par one-to-one nahin. Lekin agar domain ko \([0, \infty)\) tak mehdood (restrict) kar dein, to range par koi asar nahin parta. Is tarah \(y = \cosh x\) restricted domain \([0, \infty)\) par one-to-one aur is liye bijective ban jata hai. Chunache domain \([0, \infty)\) par inverse hyperbolic cosine function mojood hai aur hum use is tarah define karte hain:
\[x = \cosh^{-1} y \iff y = \cosh x\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Restrict kyun karna para? Line \(y = 2\) Figure 1.9 ko do jagah kaatti hai (\(x \approx -1.32\) aur \(x \approx 1.32\)). To "\(\cosh^{-1} 2\)" ke do jawab ban jate, aur function ka ek hi jawab hona chahiye. Sirf daayan hissa (\(x \ge 0\)) rakhne se har height ka ek hi jawab bachta hai, aur phir bhi 1 se upar ki har height mil jati hai, yani range poori rehti hai. Trigonometry mein aap yahi kar chuke hain: \(\sin^{-1}\) ke liye sirf \([-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}]\) lete hain.

Is Remember! box ka matlab: function ka domain inverse ki range ban jata hai, aur function ki range inverse ka domain. Is liye \(\cosh^{-1}\) ka domain \([1, \infty)\) aur range \([0, \infty)\) hai. Ab kitab ki doosri misaal:

blocks.title: Example 11
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\cosh x\) ko \([0, \infty)\) par restrict karein to woh \([1, \infty)\) par bijection hai, is liye \(\cosh^{-1} x\) \(x \ge 1\) ke liye mojood hai aur us ki values \(\ge 0\) hain.
Maloom karna (prove karna): \(\cosh^{-1} x = \ln\left(x + \sqrt{x^{2}-1}\right)\), \(x \ge 1\).
Tareeqa: bilkul Example 10 wala: \(x = \cosh y\), phir \(e^{y}\) ki quadratic, phir \(\ln\). Farq sirf aakhri faisle mein hai: is dafa dono roots positive aate hain, to sign ka faisla shart \(y \ge 0\) karegi.

Qadam 1: Inverse ko function mein badliye
\(y \in [0, \infty)\) (\(\cosh x\) ka restricted domain) aur \(x \in [1, \infty)\) (\(\cosh x\) ki range) ke liye maan lijiye
\[y = \cosh^{-1} x\]
\[x = \cosh y\]
Kyun: restricted domain par inverse ki definition. Remember! box yahi kehta hai: \(f\) ka domain \(f^{-1}\) ki range banta hai. Is liye \(y\) hamesha \(\ge 0\) hoga; yeh baat Qadam 5 mein kaam aayegi.

Qadam 2: Exponentials mein likhiye
\[x = \dfrac{e^{y} + e^{-y}}{2}\]
\[2x = e^{y} + \dfrac{1}{e^{y}}\]
Kyun: \(\cosh\) ki definition, phir dono taraf 2 se multiply, aur \(e^{-y} = \frac{1}{e^{y}}\).

Qadam 3: \(e^{y}\) ki quadratic banaiye
\[2x = \dfrac{e^{2y} + 1}{e^{y}}\]
\[2xe^{y} = e^{2y} + 1\]
\[(e^{y})^{2} - 2xe^{y} + 1 = 0\]
Kyun: \(e^{y}\) (jo kabhi zero nahin) se multiply kiya aur sab kuch ek taraf le aaye. Yahan \(a = 1\), \(b = -2x\), \(c = +1\). Example 10 se farq dekhiye: wahan \(c = -1\) tha, yahan \(+1\) hai.

Qadam 4: Quadratic formula lagaiye
\[e^{y} = \dfrac{2x \pm \sqrt{4x^{2} - 4}}{2}\]
\[e^{y} = x \pm \sqrt{x^{2}-1}\]
jahan \(x \ge 1\), \(y \ge 0\) aur \(e^{y} > 0\). Is liye
\[y = \ln\left(x \pm \sqrt{x^{2}-1}\right)\]
Kyun: \(b^{2} - 4ac = 4x^{2} - 4\), aur \(\sqrt{4x^{2}-4} = 2\sqrt{x^{2}-1}\). Yeh root real hai kyun ke \(x \ge 1\), yani \(x^{2} - 1 \ge 0\).

Qadam 5: Sahi sign chuniye
Aasani se dekha ja sakta hai ke \(x \ge 1\) ke liye \(0 < x-\sqrt{x^{2}-1} \le 1\), aur \(x > 1\) ke liye yeh 1 se sakht kam (strictly less) hai. To \(x > 1\) par \(y = \ln\left(x - \sqrt{x^{2}-1}\right) < 0\). Lekin \(y \ge 0\) chahiye, jo sirf positive sign lene se mumkin hai.
Kyun: dono roots ka product 1 hai:
\[\left(x - \sqrt{x^{2}-1}\right)\left(x + \sqrt{x^{2}-1}\right)\]
\[= x^{2} - (x^{2} - 1) = 1\]
\(x > 1\) par plus wala root 1 se bara hai, to minus wala 0 aur 1 ke darmiyan, aur 1 se chhote positive number ka \(\ln\) negative hota hai. \(x = 1\) par dono roots barabar (1) hain aur \(y = 0\), is liye plus lene se kuch nahin khota.
Dhyan dein: Example 10 mein minus root negative hone ki wajah se gaya tha; yahan woh positive hai, magar \(y \ge 0\) ki shart use nikaalti hai.

Qadam 6: Natija
\[y = \ln\left(x + \sqrt{x^{2}-1}\right)\]
\[\cosh^{-1} x = \ln\left(x + \sqrt{x^{2}-1}\right)\]
Kyun: \(y\) ki jagah wapas \(\cosh^{-1} x\) likh diya.

Tasdeeq: \(x = \frac{5}{4}\) lijiye. \(\sqrt{\frac{25}{16} - 1} = \frac{3}{4}\), to \(y = \ln\left(\frac{5}{4} + \frac{3}{4}\right) = \ln 2\), jo \(\ge 0\) hai.
\[\cosh(\ln 2) = \dfrac{2 + \frac{1}{2}}{2} = \dfrac{5}{4}\]
Wahi \(x\) wapas aa gaya. Aur \(x = 1\) par \(\ln 1 = 0\), jab ke \(\cosh 0 = 1\). Sab theek hai.
blocks.answer: \(\cosh^{-1} x = \ln\left(x + \sqrt{x^{2}-1}\right)\), tamam \(x \in [1, \infty)\) ke liye (saabit ho gaya).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab likhti hai ke \(0 < x-\sqrt{x^{2}-1} < 1\) "tamam \(x \ge 1\) ke liye". Lekin \(x = 1\) par value \(1 - 0 = 1\) hai, jo 1 se kam nahin. Sahi baat yeh hai: \(x \ge 1\) ke liye \(0 < x - \sqrt{x^{2}-1} \le 1\), aur \(x > 1\) ke liye \(< 1\). \(x = 1\) par dono signs ek hi value \(y = \ln 1 = 0\) dete hain, is liye aakhri natija \(\cosh^{-1} x = \ln\left(x + \sqrt{x^{2}-1}\right)\) bilkul sahi rehta hai.

Ab dono misaalon ko saath rakh kar dekhiye. Dono mein qadam bilkul ek jaise the: inverse ko function mein badla, exponentials mein likha, fraction khatam kar ke quadratic banai, quadratic formula lagaya, aur aakhir mein ek root chhor kar \(\ln\) liya. Jab bhi imtihan mein kisi inverse hyperbolic function ka formula saabit karne ko kaha jaye, yahi paanch qadam likhiye; examiner yahi dhoondta hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Example 10 mein minus wala root kyun gaya, aur Example 11 mein kyun? Socha? Example 10 mein \(x - \sqrt{x^{2}+1}\) negative tha, aur \(e^{y}\) negative nahin ho sakta. Example 11 mein \(x - \sqrt{x^{2}-1}\) positive hai, magar us ka \(\ln\) negative aata, jab ke restricted domain ki wajah se \(y \ge 0\) hona chahiye. Wajah alag, natija ek: plus sign.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
(Yeh misaal hamari taraf se hai.) \(\sinh^{-1}\left(\frac{4}{3}\right)\) nikaaliye:
\(\sqrt{\frac{16}{9} + 1} = \sqrt{\frac{25}{9}} = \frac{5}{3}\), to \(\sinh^{-1}\left(\frac{4}{3}\right) = \ln\left(\frac{4}{3} + \frac{5}{3}\right) = \ln 3\).
Check: \(\sinh(\ln 3) = \frac{3 - \frac{1}{3}}{2} = \frac{8/3}{2} = \frac{4}{3}\). Bilkul sahi!

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(\sinh x\) poore \(\mathbb{R}\) par bijective hai: \(\sinh^{-1} x = \ln\left(x + \sqrt{x^{2}+1}\right)\), har real \(x\) ke liye.
2. \(\cosh x\) sirf \([0, \infty)\) par restrict karne ke baad bijective hai: \(\cosh^{-1} x = \ln\left(x + \sqrt{x^{2}-1}\right)\), \(x \ge 1\), values \(\ge 0\).
3. Tareeqa: \(y = f^{-1}(x) \Rightarrow x = f(y)\); \(e^{y}\) ki quadratic; quadratic formula; na-mumkin root chhor do; \(\ln\) lo.
4. Example 10 mein minus root \(e^{y} > 0\) ki wajah se gaya; Example 11 mein \(y \ge 0\) ki wajah se.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Aakhri jawab mein dono signs \(\pm\) rakh dena: inverse function ek hi value deta hai.
2. Example 10 mein \(\sqrt{4x^{2}+4} = 2x + 2\) likhna: jama ka square root, square roots ka jama nahin hota; sahi \(2\sqrt{x^{2}+1}\) hai.
3. \(\cosh^{-1}\) ki restriction bhool jana: yeh sirf \(x \ge 1\) ke liye hai aur is ki value kabhi negative nahin.
4. Formulas mila dena: \(\sinh^{-1}\) mein root ke andar \(+1\), \(\cosh^{-1}\) mein \(-1\).
